newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki rebounds strongly, HEX clears 2,500.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki rebounds strongly, HEX clears 2,500.

text.p: Shares rallied strongly in gathering volumes on Friday, beating a weak open as enthusiasm spread through overseas markets and taking the HEX index through key resistance as a start-of-year rally emerged, brokers said.
The HEX, already probing new all-time highs at the end of 1996, made a convincing break through the psychological 2,500 barrier to end active trade up over one percent at 2,517.20.
"The outlook for the stock market at the start of the year is really upbeat -- there seems to be a flood of liquidity into shares," one broker said.

Telecoms major Nokia closed up 3.50 markka at 267.50, boosted by an early techs rally in the U.S., but attention was more widely spread with strong gains in construction stocks again featuring amid more upbeat news from the companies.
"Construction shares have been in hot demand today -- it clearly signals strong economic growth in general," one broker said. But demand for construction issues was mainly domestic.
Builder Starckjohann hit a two-year high, up 0.30 markka at 7.75, after saying its 1997 profit would be clearly better.

Media group Aamulehti also rose sharply, ending up 10.00 markka or over seven percent at 150.00 after it said Swedish media group Marieberg had raised its holding in it to over 20 percent as a result of bond conversion.
Marieberg repeated that it had no plans increase its stake further, but brokers said the news had fuelled speculation that it would.
